clue.text: Doubly outstanding damage, superficially

parts.note: the clue wants two words for 'outstanding'; the first is slang def, meaning excellent
an ace performance is an outstanding one

explanation.surface: Something remarkable twice over turns out to have only surface damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' means two different words for outstanding are wanted, the first being hip-hop slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil the surface or appearance of something, as vandals do to a wall, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Girton's top dons reach conclusion on blessed fellow's summary

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
to don is to put on, so the end word is worn around the letter

parts.note: to die is to come to an end

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue

parts.note: ST is a saint, a blessed person

explanation.surface: Cambridge college academics finish their summary of a saint's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Girton is a Cambridge college; 'dons' there are its academics, but here it means wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of written material.

clue.text: Oldest trees divided, bushes primarily retained

parts.note: firs are conifers

indicators.note: the split word holds the letter inside itself

parts.note: torn means split or divided

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter of bushes is taken

explanation.surface: Ancient trees are split apart, with shrubs mainly kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child of a family is the one born before the rest.

clue.text: About to jettison plane's passenger section

parts.note: CA is circa, about
to bin is to throw away

explanation.surface: An aircraft about to dump its passenger area.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment of an aircraft where travellers sit is called this.

clue.text: Compares singular food and drink

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
tack is old slang for food, as in hard tack
to sup is to drink, especially in sips

explanation.surface: A diner weighs up one item of food against one drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that holds up when measured against another thing is said to match or compare well.

clue.text: Novel outings — no parking required, with public transport available

indicators.note: no parking means the letter for parking is left out

parts.note: trips are outings
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
trams are city street railcars
handy means close by and available

explanation.surface: Trips that need no parking because trams are close by.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristram Shandy is the eighteenth-century comic novel by Laurence Sterne.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the famously digressive eighteenth-century novel by Laurence Sterne.

clue.text: Horse involved in accident after tailing vehicle

indicators.note: the horse is wrapped up inside what follows
tailing means docking the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: chance means accident, luck
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse is caught up in an accident after following a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after tailing' drops the last letter, leaving CHANC. A charabanc is an old open motor coach once used for day trips in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an early open-topped coach used for outings, popular in Britain a century ago.

clue.text: Holy man raising current crops — for birds

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting from bottom to top, so read upwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
maws are stomachs or crops of birds and animals

explanation.surface: A holy man raises a current of crops to feed birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for birds' points to the crop, the throat pouch of a bird, rather than farm produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher or ascetic is given this title.

clue.text: Pass water round mine, on descent

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: pee is to urinate
a dig is an excavation
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A miner relieves himself around the pit on the way down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage or ancestry is one's line of descent.

clue.text: Lawyer's leader in conflict with judge — evidence of disaster in case?

indicators.note: the leader letter is placed in the conflict word

parts.note: a fight is a conflict

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of the word

parts.note: a recorder is a part-time judge in English courts

explanation.surface: A barrister clashes with a judge over evidence in a disastrous case.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case' is the box housing the black box after a crash, not a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The crash-proof box in aircraft that records data is examined after disasters.

clue.text: Serviceman stabbed by a scurrilous patriot

indicators.note: something stabbed has another thing pushed into it, so the serviceman is cut open by the next words

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarsely or irreverently humorous

explanation.surface: A soldier is attacked by a foul-mouthed nationalist.
explanation.walkthrough: GARIBALDI was the Italian patriot who led the unification of Italy; the biscuit named after him is a British favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Giuseppe Garibaldi is a famous Italian nationalist hero of the Risorgimento.

clue.text: Retired lawman receiving fresh commendation

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the lawman takes in the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: DA is a US district attorney
raw means fresh or uncooked

explanation.surface: A former police officer is given a new honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' gives DRAWA before 'Retired' turns it round. A DA is an American district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prize or honour given in recognition is a form of official praise.

clue.text: Agreed on Chinese taking part

indicators.note: only a part of the words Chinese taking is used, the letters running across the word gap

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to join in with a Chinese takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A set price or set date is one fixed and agreed upon in advance.

clue.text: Clearing books one has stopped cancelling

indicators.note: the books and one plug the cancelling word like a stopper, sitting inside it

parts.note: negating means cancelling out
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper clears accounts, having halted a cancellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting past an obstacle, as a horse does a fence, is a less common sense of the word.

clue.text: Hunted species picked up by some

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than read, and only by speakers who drop the r

parts.note: a sort is a kind or species

explanation.surface: A hunted animal species is noticed by a few people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by some' admits the match works only in a non-rhotic accent, as in southern England, where the r is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Searched for or pursued is the past tense of seek, matching the past participle of hunt.

clue.text: Voucher for university pinched by arrogant drunk

indicators.note: pinched means gripped, so the university is squeezed inside the other letters
a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A sponsor for a university is robbed by a drunken arrogant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who vouches for, or underwrites, another's debts or obligations.

clue.text: Going round, express a word of thanks in a single go

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the pieces are read from the end

parts.note: to emit is to give out or express
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A traveller on a tour says thank you all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' turns EMITATA backwards. TA is the British colloquial thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing things together, simultaneously, rather than spread out over several occasions.

clue.text: Like Dead Ringers broadcast in dialect

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The impressions show Dead Ringers goes out in regional accents.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead Ringers is a British radio and TV impressionists' comedy show; a dead ringer is an exact lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact lookalikes are the same as each other in appearance.

clue.text: Bringing up the rear, despite one's efforts?

definitions.meaning: in spite of what was done or expected

explanation.surface: Coming last, despite trying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it means behind everybody; as an idiom it means nevertheless.

clue.text: Stirring music from remote East introduced by devotee

indicators.note: the devotee comes first, leading in the rest

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or devotee
far means distant or remote
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Rousing music from the Far East is presented by an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets announcing someone is a rousing musical call.

clue.text: Fish, one to be had without difficulty

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of North America with a mouth for feeding on the bottom

definitions.text: one to be had without difficulty
definitions.meaning: a gullible person easily fooled, someone 'had' or conned

explanation.surface: A fish that is easily caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe or gull is easily taken in; a mouth-feeding fish shares the name.

clue.text: Radio officer finding space for recreation aboard

indicators.note: the recreation space finds itself placed within the ship, so it goes inside

parts.note: being aboard means being on a steamship, abbreviated SS
a park is an area for recreation

explanation.surface: A ship's radio operator finds room on deck to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is not in the clue: 'aboard' implies it, a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional nickname for a ship's wireless operator.

clue.text: Project inserting second bit of tooth into spare denture

parts.note: extra means spare or additional

indicators.note: a letter is placed into the following words, as if pushed in

parts.note: a plate is a set of false teeth

indicators.note: the second letter of the word tooth is taken

explanation.surface: A dentist fits a bit of a tooth into a spare set of false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' is the verb, not the noun; a plate is the British term for a denture.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate future values by extending a trend is a synonym for forecasting or projecting.

clue.text: Auditor's monitored land area

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the next word is as heard

parts.note: tracked means followed or monitored

explanation.surface: An accountant's survey of a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch or expanse of land is a synonym, as in a tract of forest.

clue.text: Sporting contest opening online, as it were?

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in email
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A sports match starts streaming online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were?' hints that an online opening is an e-vent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a single competition on a sports programme, such as the high jump.

clue.text: Provide clue for little reward

definitions.meaning: to give a hint or inside information
a small gratuity left for a waiter

explanation.surface: Give a hint in exchange for a small gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint and a gratuity both share this short word, one as a verb, one as a noun.

clue.text: Bill likely to change

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill posted up
apt means likely or inclined, as in apt to fail

explanation.surface: A legislative bill will probably be amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' here is a poster, not a law.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to modify or adjust something to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Rebel comrade commandeering chief exec's bashed vehicle

indicators.note: the shuffled letters seize and hold the chief executive inside them
to rebel is to rise up against order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: DG is a director-general, a chief executive

explanation.surface: A rebellious comrade seizes the boss's car and crashes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel' rearranges the comrade into DO EMCAR so the boss can sit between DO and EMCAR. A dodgem is a fairground bumper car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairground bumper cars are designed to be bashed into each other.

clue.text: Actually preferring rapper's introduction to two lines in formal language

indicators.note: one thing is chosen over another, so a letter is swapped in for the two lines

parts.note: literally means actually or in fact
L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word rapper's is used

explanation.surface: A rapper genuinely prefers lyrics in a formal style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preferring ... to' swaps R in for LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Words suited to writing rather than speech are bookish or formal in register.

clue.text: Input device's phraseology almost American

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: style is a way of expressing oneself, phraseology
US means American

explanation.surface: A writing tool's manner of expression is nearly American.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen used on a touchscreen tablet to enter data or draw.
